questionsToConsider: How many revision rounds are included in your standard price?
Do you handle print production, or hand over files only?
Do you write copy, or should clients bring their own?
Which file formats do you deliver by default?
guide.howToUseResponses: Price from the quantity and the brand answer together. Ten social graphics for a client with guidelines is production work, while one logo for a client with nothing yet is the start of an identity project and deserves a different quote. If the copy isn't ready, either add writing to the quote or make the deadline depend on receiving final text.
customizeSteps: Edit the list of design pieces to match what you offer, and remove the ones you don't take on.
Change the budget ranges to fit your rates, and say in the ending how many revision rounds a quote includes.
Link to the form from your portfolio and social profiles, and read the briefs in the dashboard.

faqs.q: What should a graphic design quote form ask?
faqs.a: What pieces are needed and how many sizes, what brand material exists, whether the copy is ready, where it will be used and the deadline. Budget as a range helps too.

faqs.q: Why ask whether the copy is ready?
faqs.a: Designing around placeholder text often means redoing layouts later. Knowing up front lets you quote for writing or set the schedule around the final text.

faqs.q: How do I price print design differently?
faqs.a: Print work needs exact sizes, bleed and often a proof check with the printer. This form asks print clients for sizes and quantities so you can include that time.

faqs.q: Can clients upload their logo and brand files?
faqs.a: Yes. Clients who already have a brand are asked to upload their logo and guidelines in the form.
